title: Visual support board
description: The contract the Composer agent must return and the Reviewer agent validates. Authority for field names is SPEC.md section 3; authority for the example is SPEC.md section 5.

outcome.description: ENVELOPE FIELD, not part of the board. The Composer prompt requires it (prompts/composer.md:305 for a board, :66 for a referral) and it is how the caller tells a board from a refusal before reading anything else. Added 9 Nov 2026 after the FIRST REAL BOARD from the published app failed this schema: the prompt required outcome and reasoning, the schema had neither, and additionalProperties is false. Optional rather than required because the four fixtures predate it.

reasoning.description: ENVELOPE FIELD, not part of the board. Two sentences for the parent: why this support type, and why this Then. Required by prompts/composer.md:344 and written to the Board row, never rendered on a printed card. Added 9 Nov 2026 with outcome, same reason.

supportType.description: Which of the four layout templates. Decides the permitted card count, see allOf below.

title.description: Shown to the parent, not to the child. Full sentences are fine here; the three-word rule applies only to card labels.

theme.description: Drawn from Child.SpecialInterests. REQUIRED. Never null and never omitted -- when no theme can be derived, the value is the sentinel "TBD" and themeNote must say what the Composer needs or recommends. null and an absent key both mean 'unknown or forgotten' and cannot be told apart; "TBD" is a statement. An invented theme is still invalid.

script.description: One or two low-demand phrases per phase. Every phase in the enum must appear exactly once.

evidenceBasis.description: Which National Standards (2009) Established Treatments this board rests on, each with the specific technique within it. A closed list is the point: it is what stops a model inventing a twelfth practice. The enum here is the SIX this application can honestly claim, not all eleven -- a First-Then board cannot rest on Peer Training Package. All eleven remain in the EvidencePractice static entity as the reference table. Names are verbatim from the legend under Table 3 of the National Standards Report.

technique.description: The named technique within that package, from the report's own examples.

enum: responsive education and prelinguistic milieu teaching

citations.description: Where the layout came from, named so a clinician can check it. Free text, because the source is a document and a section, not an identifier.

agentRunId.description: Written by the platform, not the model. Present on a stored board, absent on a freshly returned one.

themeNote.description: Required when theme is "TBD", and only meaningful then. One sentence in which the Composer does ONE of three things: asks the parent a specific question that would yield a theme, recommends a theme to try, or states why this board is better plain. This is the exception path the whole TBD convention exists for -- a board that cannot be themed should say so and say what would fix it, not fall silent.

sensorySupports.description: Which regulation tools this board tells the parent to have ready, drawn from the child's own kit. PORTED 7 Nov 2026 from the other session's AGENT-1 prompt, which had an enumerable Sensory Safety Kit where this project had only free-text sensoryNotes -- a closed list the Composer can act on, the Reviewer can cross-check against triggers, and the card library can illustrate. Name only tools the profile says the child HAS; a board that calls for headphones the family does not own is a board that fails on first use. Optional and often empty: most boards need none, and listing tools for the sake of it is the failure mode here. SunflowerLanyard is the hidden-disabilities lanyard, which signals to strangers rather than regulating the child -- it belongs on a board about being out, not about brushing teeth.

sensorySupportOther.description: One tool this child uses that the eight do not cover -- a weighted lap pad, a particular cup, a sibling's hoodie. The enum is a closed list on purpose so the common case is checkable; this is the escape hatch so the uncommon case is not silently dropped. Name the object, not its purpose.

label.description: GUARDRAIL 1, three words maximum, enforced structurally here as well as in code. The pattern counts space-separated tokens: one to three. A hyphenated compound is one word by this rule, which is a deliberate decision recorded in GUARDRAILS.md.

imagePrompt.description: Never contains the child's name: prompts say 'a child'. That cannot be checked here, because the schema does not hold the profile, so it is a code guardrail. SPEC.md section 5.

altText.description: Required, because a visual support with no alternative text excludes the screen-reader user it was meant to include.

phrase.description: Fewest words wins. The cap is characters rather than words because a phrase is spoken, not printed on a card.

promptHierarchy.description: Least intrusive first. Levels must start at 1 and be contiguous, which the schema cannot express; GUARDRAILS.md rule 8 covers it in code.

boardAction.description: What the parent does with their HANDS, which no other field covers. placement says where the board lives, promptHierarchy says how to prompt, script says what to say -- none of them say to move a card. Both cards stay visible from the start, because the child has to see what they are working for; the First card comes OFF when the first activity is finished, and the parent points to the Then. Leaving both cards up for the whole routine is a picture of two things that are both true, which is a choice board. The sequence is carried by the card moving. Required for the two support types that have cards to move, see allOf below.

childChoice.description: One sentence naming a decision that belongs to the CHILD -- which of two Thens they work for, which order two equal steps go in, where the board hangs. Ported 7 Nov 2026 from the other session's interactive checkpoints, and it lands on machinery this project already had: Choice is a card Role and 'choice' is a technique under Antecedent Package. Optional. THE FIRST IS NEVER THE CHOICE -- the board rests on the First happening, and nothing here lets a child decline the task. Offer only choices the adult will honour; a choice overruled is worse than one never offered.

generalization.description: How this board moves on: another setting, another adult, or a HARDER version of the same routine. The second kind was added 8 November 2026 and has a specific shape worth naming. When a First-Then board becomes easy, the next step is NOT a six-card schedule -- it is FIRST, THEN, THEN: one more small step before the same reward. A practising speech pathologist describes exactly that progression, and our four support types jump straight from two cards to four-to-eight with nothing in between. Say it here in a sentence rather than building a fifth layout for it.

allOf.description: GUARDRAIL 4 and GUARDRAIL 3 for First-Then: exactly two cards, and one of them must be the Then card. The reward is structural, so this is a schema rule and not only a code rule.
GUARDRAIL 4: a visual schedule is 4 to 8 cards. Fewer is not a schedule; more overwhelms the child it was built for.

A social narrative may be pure text OR illustrated, one picture per page. SPEC.md section 2 wrote its card count as "n/a", which the schema first read as ZERO and the eval set read as "no fixed range" -- the two disagreed for eleven days before anyone noticed. A.J. settled it on 8 November 2026: the schema was the wrong reading. A story for a child whose visualStyle is Icons SHOULD be illustrated, and SocialNarrative being the one support type with nothing to look at is an odd thing for a visual supports app to ship. The range is 0 to 8 rather than the 4 to 8 first proposed, because forcing four pictures onto a narrative that works as text would be the same mistake in the other direction.

A board whose cards never move teaches simultaneity rather than sequence, so the two support types that HAVE cards to move must say what to do with them. ParameterCards are shown and put away rather than worked through, and a SocialNarrative carries no cards at all, so neither is required to carry this field and neither should invent one.

The TBD exception path. A board with no derivable theme must say what it needs: a question for the parent, a recommendation, or the reason plain is better. Without this block "TBD" would be a silent shrug, which is the thing null already did badly.
